clue.text: Crewmen decorate manually

parts.note: to deck a room is to decorate it
something done manually is done with the hands

explanation.surface: Sailors are told to paint and dress up the ship by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary sailors working on a ship's deck are the crew members known by this name.

clue.text: Converted front of 1 ac into rear

definitions.text: Converted front of 1 ac into rear

parts.words: Converted front of 1 ac into rear
parts.note: the front half of the answer to 1 across is a pack of cards, its rear half the players' holdings: cards passed from the pack to the players have been given out

explanation.surface: An instruction to change the start of a word into its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across splits into DECK and HANDS; turning the deck into hands is what a card dealer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards distributed from the pack to the players have been given out in this way, the past tense of deal.

clue.text: Collected writings, excluding the novel?

parts.note: a notebook of collected quotations and jottings, read jokingly as a volume containing only the ordinary and nothing new or novel

explanation.surface: An anthology of someone's writings that leaves out their fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a work of fiction but means 'new': a book of the commonplace excludes anything novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A notebook in which a reader copies out quotations and passages is a traditional collection of writings.

clue.text: It's repeatedly exemplified in Crown Derby

definitions.text: It's repeatedly exemplified in Crown Derby

parts.words: It's repeatedly exemplified in Crown Derby
parts.note: a crown and a derby (bowler hat) are both things worn on the head, so the category is exemplified twice

explanation.surface: A motif recurs on pieces of Crown Derby porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain, but here 'Crown' and 'Derby' are two kinds of hat; a derby is the American name for a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowns and derby hats are both examples of things worn on the head, the general term for hats.

clue.text: Legal officials, as Leo and ten others are

parts.words: as Leo and ten others are
parts.note: Leo and ten other zodiac signs make eleven signs that are not the Ram

parts.words: as Leo and ten others are
parts.note: the twelfth sign, the Ram, is the one these eleven are not

explanation.surface: A lion and ten companions share some qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: There are twelve signs of the zodiac, so Leo and ten others are every sign but one: they are NOT ARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are public officials who certify documents and witness signatures for legal purposes.

clue.text: Lavish friends, cryptically indicated

parts.note: read as wordplay in a down entry, a word for slap written upwards gives pals, meaning friends

explanation.surface: Generous companions, described in a riddling way.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, SLAP 'up' (written backwards in a down light) giving PALS, which the clue calls 'friends'; 'cryptically indicated' warns of this.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, lavishly generous one, an informal British idiom.

clue.text: Toast the great soprano

definitions.meaning: Dame Nellie ... was a celebrated Australian soprano

explanation.definitionFit: Thin dry toast was named after the singer Nellie Melba, who is also the soprano meant.

clue.text: Complaint from aristocratic bluestocking?

parts.note: a bluestocking is a learned woman, so one with a Master of Arts degree, MA
a lady is a woman of aristocratic rank

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a well-born intellectual woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order: an aristocratic bluestocking is a LADY with an MA, written MA LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, and a complaint in the medical sense is the same thing.

clue.text: Reasoning that's unorthodox, but never back-to front?

definitions.meaning: thinking that approaches a problem from an unexpected angle
thought that goes sideways, never moving in the back-to-front direction

explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is problem solving by indirect, unconventional approaches, and lateral means sideways rather than front to back.

clue.text: Flier offering a way to support new opera

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece supports the one above it
new means the letters of opera are made into something fresh

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way

explanation.surface: A plane provides a route to back a fresh operatic production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OPERA as EROP; 'to support' puts LANE beneath A + EROP in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane is a flying machine, so a flier in the sense of something that flies.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps, many represented in paintings

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit within the word for paintings

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

indicators.note: represented means the letters of many are presented in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A military figure among the many portrayed on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' turns MANY into MYAN, which goes 'in' ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants have a soldier caste, so a soldier ant may be an example of this insect.

clue.text: In football, starting with the best players

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits within the words football and starting

explanation.surface: A football team that begins with its finest players on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star team or cast is one made up entirely of top performers.

clue.text: Lash, however, no good when cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the word for however loses its ending

parts.note: though can mean however

explanation.surface: A whip, though useless once trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last three letters of the word for however, leaving its informal written form; 'Lash' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a thin strip of leather, such as the lash of a whip.

clue.text: I'd run port differently for this kind of voyage

indicators.note: arranged differently means the letters of I'd run port are put in another order

explanation.surface: A traveller plans to sail to a harbour by another route.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey out and back again, a kind of voyage.

clue.text: Spraying it could make a part wet

definitions.text: Spraying it could make a part wet

indicators.note: spraying scatters things, so the letters of a part wet are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Spraying with it could wet one area.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: water from the tap, sprayed about, could indeed wet part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the household tap is what you would spray to wet something, and the whole clue describes that.

clue.text: When converted, try to pray — it's said they did in C of E

definitions.text: When converted, try to pray — it's said they did in C of E

indicators.note: converted means the letters of try to pray are changed into a new form, a pun on religious conversion

explanation.surface: Newly converted believers attempt prayer, as Anglicans are said to have done.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is that 'the Church of England is the Tory Party at prayer'; the Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservatives are the political group of which the Church of England was famously called the praying form.

clue.text: Perform as runner, say, or high-jumper

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a homophone

parts.note: to flee is to run away, acting as a runner

explanation.surface: An athlete competes on the track or in the high jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' and 'high-jumper' suggest athletics, but the runner is one who flees and the jumper is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is an insect famous for jumping enormously high relative to its size.

clue.text: Some of it gets blanket coverage

definitions.text: Some of it gets blanket coverage

parts.words: Some of it gets blanket coverage
parts.note: sheets and pillowcases on a bed are literally covered by a blanket, punning on news coverage

explanation.surface: Part of a story gets comprehensive media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blanket coverage' suggests thorough reporting, but a blanket lies over the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen means sheets and pillowcases, and the sheets lie under the blanket.

clue.text: Weapon that makes quarrel potentially fatal

definitions.text: Weapon that makes quarrel potentially fatal

parts.words: Weapon that makes quarrel potentially fatal
parts.note: a quarrel is also the short bolt fired by a particular medieval weapon, so this weapon makes a quarrel deadly

explanation.surface: A gun that turns an argument into something deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument but is the square-headed bolt shot from this weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow that shoots short bolts called quarrels.

clue.text: Studied Communist's pronouncement

indicators.note: pronouncement means the word is heard spoken, giving a homophone

parts.note: Red is a common word for a Communist

explanation.surface: A party member has studied a political statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense of read is said like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have read a subject, especially at university, is to have studied it.

clue.text: A sort of cashmere? I don't know!

indicators.note: a sort of means the letters of cashmere are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure what type of wool a garment is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an informal exclamation meaning that the speaker has no idea.

clue.text: Symphony's opening with slow movement that's carelessly written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a crawl is slow movement

explanation.surface: A symphony begins with a slow movement whose score is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow movement' looks like a musical term but means a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is something written hastily and untidily, handwriting done carelessly.

clue.text: Relax here in warmth, extreme in the centre

indicators.note: in means the word for extreme is placed inside the word for the centre

parts.note: a hub is a centre
OTT, over the top, means extreme

explanation.surface: A warm place to unwind, with extremes kept in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relax here in warmth' is the definition; the second 'in' is the container signal, and 'extreme' is the over-the-top abbreviation, not an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a heated outdoor bath for relaxing in, a warm place to unwind.

clue.text: Prior to one's first-class debut?

parts.note: describes the stage of a child's education before the first class at school, not a sports debut

explanation.surface: A cricketer's career before playing first-class cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class cricket is the top level of the long-form game; here 'first class' is a child's first class at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Preschool describes the time before a child starts school and attends a first class.

clue.text: So-called boy's cheerful sound

indicators.note: so-called means the word is as it is called aloud, a homophone
sound means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sonny is a familiar way to address a boy

explanation.surface: A lad's cheerful voice is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny disposition is a cheerful, bright and happy one.

clue.text: Our state in that part of Canada

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for our state goes inside the word for that

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
for a British newspaper, our state is the UK

explanation.surface: A British citizen describes their country within a Canadian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a British paper, so 'our state' means Britain's own abbreviation; 'that' in its archaic form takes it 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukon is a territory in north-western Canada.

clue.text: In Brazilian city, diplomat's skill used to control disorder

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
tact is the skill of a diplomat

explanation.surface: A diplomat calms trouble in Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to order crowds to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was legislation proclaimed to disperse crowds, a measure for controlling disorder.

clue.text: Club that may improve a writer's flow

definitions.meaning: an old golf club with a lofted head

definitions.text: that may improve a writer's flow
definitions.meaning: licking the nib of a pen helps the ink to run

explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a golf club, and a nib lick would help ink flow.

clue.text: Countryman joined farm animals beside lake

parts.note: a yoke is a pair of oxen joined together
L is an abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A farmer harnessed cattle by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is a naive or unsophisticated rural person, a disparaging word for a countryman.

clue.text: In vehicle

parts.note: in meaning fashionable: a cart for musicians that everyone climbs on to follow a trend

explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a wagon carrying a band, and to jump on it is to join a fashionable cause.
